title: Introduction to Neural Networks
content: Neural networks are computing systems inspired by biological neural networks. They consist of interconnected nodes called neurons that process information using connectionist approaches. Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks for complex pattern recognition.
author: John Smith

title: Transformer Architecture
content: The Transformer is a deep learning architecture introduced in 2017. It relies entirely on self-attention mechanisms to compute representations of input and output. It has become the foundation for modern NLP models like BERT and GPT.
author: Alan Turing

title: FAISS Vector Search
content: FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. It contains algorithms that search in sets of vectors of any size. It is developed by Facebook AI Research and supports GPU acceleration.
author: Meta AI

title: Sentence Embeddings
content: Sentence embeddings convert sentences into fixed-size vectors that capture semantic meaning. Models like Sentence-BERT allow efficient similarity comparison between sentences using cosine similarity.
author: Sarah Johnson

title: BERT Overview
content: BERT is a pre-trained transformer model designed for NLP tasks. It uses bidirectional training to understand context from both left and right. BERT can be fine-tuned for tasks like question answering and sentiment analysis.
author: Google AI

title: Cross-Encoder Reranking
content: Cross-encoders jointly encode a pair of sentences to produce a relevance score. They are more accurate than bi-encoders for re-ranking tasks but are slower since they process each pair independently.
author: Mike Chen

title: Cosine Similarity
content: Cosine similarity measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors. It is commonly used in information retrieval and text mining to compare document similarity. Values range from -1 to 1.
author: David Brown

title: Dense Passage Retrieval
content: DPR is a retrieval method that uses dense embeddings for passages. It trains two BERT models - one for encoding questions and another for encoding passages - to maximize similarity of relevant pairs.
author: Facebook AI

title: Quantum Computing Basics
content: Quantum computing uses quantum bits or qubits that can exist in superposition states. Unlike classical bits that are either 0 or 1 qubits can be both simultaneously enabling parallel computation.
author: Emily Zhang

title: Reinforcement Learning
content: Reinforcement learning is an area of machine learning where agents learn by interacting with their environment. The agent receives rewards or penalties based on actions taken and learns to maximize cumulative reward.
author: Richard Sutton

title: Natural Language Processing
content: NLP is a branch of AI that helps computers understand and generate human language. Applications include translation sentiment analysis chatbots and text summarization.
author: MIT OpenCourseWare

title: Graph Neural Networks
content: GNNs are a class of neural networks that operate on graph data. They learn representations by aggregating information from neighboring nodes. Applications include social network analysis and molecular property prediction.
author: Stanford AI

title: Computer Vision
content: Computer vision enables machines to interpret visual information from the world. Techniques include convolutional neural networks object detection and image segmentation. Applications range from autonomous vehicles to medical imaging.
author: Fei-Fei Li

title: Attention Mechanism
content: The attention mechanism allows models to focus on relevant parts of the input when producing output. It computes weighted combinations of values where weights are determined by compatibility between query and key.
author: Google Brain

title: Transfer Learning
content: Transfer learning leverages knowledge gained from solving one problem to solve a different but related problem. Pre-trained models can be fine-tuned with smaller datasets saving time and computational resources.
author: Andrew Ng
